items.claim: attrs follows Calendar Versioning (CalVer).
items.label: supported
items.reason: Version markers throughout the source (e.g. 19.2.0, 21.3.0, 25.4.0, 26.2.0) are year-based, which is CalVer.

items.claim: Setting the annotations before the build would have made `_transform_attrs` read them as auto-attribs declarations.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: `make_class` passes `these=cls_dict`, and `_transform_attrs` takes the `these is not None` branch so annotations are never interpreted as auto-attribs declarations; the complaint would instead come from `from_counting_attr`'s "Type annotation and type argument cannot both be present" check.

items.claim: `_has_own_attribute` is implemented as `attrib_name in cls.__dict__`, checking only the class's own dict rather than its MRO.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The function body is literally `return attrib_name in cls.__dict__`, which ignores the MRO.

items.claim: `@attr.s` is aliased as `@attr.attributes`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `s = attributes = attrs` makes `attr.attributes` an alias of `attr.s`.

items.claim: `make_class` applies the decorator as `_attrs(these=cls_dict, **attributes_arguments)(type_)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: That exact call is present in `make_class`.

items.claim: `add_repr` calls `_make_repr_script`, which returns a source string and a globals dict.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `add_repr` does `script, globs = _make_repr_script(self._attrs, ns)` and `_make_repr_script` returns the joined source string plus the globs dict.

items.claim: `Attribute` defines `__setattr__` to raise `FrozenInstanceError`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Attribute.__setattr__` raises `FrozenInstanceError`.

items.claim: `Factory`'s `takes_self` parameter defaults to `False`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `def __init__(self, factory, takes_self=False)` confirms the default.

items.claim: The attrs `attrs` namespace is built on top of the `attr` logic internally.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `attrs` package simply re-exports objects imported from `attr` and `attr._make`/`attr._next_gen`.

items.claim: `_ClassBuilder.__init__` puts `__attrs_attrs__` and `__attrs_props__` into the class dict.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both `__attrs_attrs__` and `__attrs_props__` are stored in `self._cls_dict`.

items.claim: `_create_slots_class` walks the new class's dict, unwrapping classmethods, staticmethods and properties, and overwrites any closure cell whose contents are the old class.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The loop chains `cls.__dict__.values()` with extra functions, unwraps classmethod/staticmethod via `__func__` and property via `fget`, and assigns `cell.cell_contents = cls` on a match with the old class.

items.claim: `FrozenInstanceError` is raised when a `frozen=True` class is modified.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Frozen classes get `_frozen_setattrs` installed as `__setattr__`, which raises `FrozenInstanceError`.

items.claim: `astuple`'s `recurse` parameter defaults to `True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `astuple(inst, recurse=True, ...)` defaults recurse to True.

items.claim: Slotted classes do not have a `__dict__` and prevent adding new attributes at runtime that weren't defined in `__slots__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The slots class builder strips `__dict__` and sets `__slots__`, and the glossary demonstrates the resulting AttributeError on unknown attributes.

items.claim: The attrs benchmark suite measures `__eq__`, `__hash__`, `asdict`, and `astuple`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The contents of the benchmark file were not shown, so its measured operations can't be checked.

items.claim: `_generate_unique_filename` appends a counter when the candidate filename is already taken by different source.
items.label: contradicted
items.reason: `_generate_unique_filename` just formats a string; the collision counter logic lives in `_linecache_and_compile`.

items.claim: `optional(validator)` allows the value to be `None` or satisfy the provided validator.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_OptionalValidator.__call__` returns early for None and otherwise delegates to the wrapped validator.

items.claim: `attrs.inspect` is documented as experimental and outside the project's backwards-compatibility guarantee.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The `inspect` docstring warns the feature is experimental and not covered by the strict backwards-compatibility guarantees.

items.claim: `Converter(takes_self=True)` enables a converter function to be called as `fn(val, self)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: With takes_self and not takes_field, the converter is called as `self.converter(value, instance)`.

items.claim: The `field_transformer` hook receives the class being decorated and a list of `Attribute` objects.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `field_transformer(cls, attrs)` is called with the class and the collected Attribute objects.

items.claim: The `Converter` class can be configured with `takes_self` and `takes_field` parameters.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `Converter.__init__` accepts keyword-only `takes_self` and `takes_field`.

items.claim: For a mandatory field with no factory and no converter, the alias is added to `args` as a bare positional parameter and `_assign('a', 'a', False)` returns `'self.a = a'`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The final else-branch appends the bare `arg_name` to `args` and calls `fmt_setter`, which for non-frozen classes is `_assign`, yielding `self.a = a`.

items.claim: Annotations wrapped in `typing.ClassVar` are ignored by the attrs attribute collection process.
items.label: supported
items.reason: In auto_attribs collection, annotations matching ClassVar prefixes are skipped.

items.claim: The pre-commit `interrogate` hook ensures the `tests` directory maintains docstring coverage.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: The pre-commit configuration file's contents were not shown.

items.claim: `converters.optional` returns `None` directly for `None` values without calling the wrapped converter.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both optional_converter variants return None immediately when val is None, before invoking the wrapped converter.

items.claim: The tox `docs-watch` environment uses `watchfiles` to trigger rebuilds when source or documentation files change.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: tox.ini contents were not shown, so the docs-watch environment can't be checked.

items.claim: `_determine_setters(frozen=False, slots=False, base_attr_map={})` returns `((), _assign, _assign_with_converter)` because `slots` is irrelevant when the class is not frozen.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `slots` is only consulted inside the `frozen is True` branch; otherwise the function returns `(), _assign, _assign_with_converter`.

items.claim: In Python, objects that compare equal must have the same hash.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The hashing docs state that two equal objects must have the same hash.

items.claim: Validators are attached to attributes using the `validator` parameter in `attrs.field()` or `attr.ib()`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both `attrib` and `field` take a `validator` parameter used to attach validators.

items.claim: In `asdict`, when `filter` is None the per-field skip check does not fire and when `value_serializer` is None the serializer hook does not run.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The skip only happens `if filter is not None and not filter(a, v)` and the serializer only runs `if value_serializer is not None`.

items.claim: `_compile_and_eval()` compiles the generated script into bytecode.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_compile_and_eval` calls `compile(script, filename, "exec")` and evals the resulting bytecode.

items.claim: The generated `__setattr__` looks the field up in a dict and, if the hook is a generator function, drives it around the assignment.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The generated `__setattr__` does `a, hook, is_gen = sa_attrs[name]` and, when `is_gen()`, calls `next(gen)`, sets the attribute, then resumes the generator.

items.claim: When a type annotation is present, it is stored in `Attribute.type`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The annotation is passed to `Attribute.from_counting_attr` as `type` and stored on the Attribute's `type` slot.

items.claim: `_is_class_var` stringifies the annotation, strips surrounding quotes, and tests `annot.startswith(_CLASSVAR_PREFIXES)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The function converts to `str`, strips surrounding quotes, and returns `annot.startswith(_CLASSVAR_PREFIXES)`.

items.claim: `_transform_attrs` ensures no mandatory attributes follow attributes with default values.
items.label: supported
items.reason: _transform_attrs raises ValueError if a mandatory attribute follows one with a default.

items.claim: `_collect_base_attrs_broken` walks the MRO forward instead of reversed, keeps attributes already marked `inherited`, and mutates the `taken_attr_names` set it was given.
items.label: supported
items.reason: It iterates `cls.__mro__[1:-1]` (not reversed), filters only on `taken_attr_names`, and mutates that set with `taken_attr_names.add(a.name)`.

items.claim: attrs classes automatically generate `__match_args__` based on the attribute order to support structural pattern matching.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `add_match_args` builds `__match_args__` as a tuple of field names (in attribute order) for init, non-kw_only fields, and is applied when match_args is true.

items.claim: The generated `__repr__` renders the class name from `self.__class__.__qualname__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: With the default `ns is None`, the class-name fragment is `{self.__class__.__qualname__.rsplit(">.", 1)[-1]}`.

items.claim: When no `__attrs_pre_init__` exists, `_ClassBuilder.__init__` makes no `inspect.signature` call and leaves the hook flags False.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_pre_init_has_args` is initialized to False and the `import inspect` / `inspect.signature` block is guarded by `if self._has_pre_init:`.

items.claim: NFKC normalization is the same normalization the Python parser applies to identifiers.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The code comment states "Class identifiers are converted into the normal form NFKC while parsing", which is why `make_class` applies NFKC.

items.claim: `attrs` performs its work at class definition time via code generation, minimizing runtime impact at instantiation.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The builder compiles generated method scripts once at class-definition time and the docs state everything happens exactly once when the class is defined with no runtime cost afterwards.

items.claim: `evolve` works with frozen classes because it calls the constructor rather than mutating the instance.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `evolve` collects init values and calls `cls(**changes)`, creating a new instance via `__init__` rather than mutating, which works for frozen classes.

items.claim: `converters.default_if_none` replaces `None` values with a static default value or the result of a factory function.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `default_if_none` returns a converter replacing None with the given default or the result of `Factory(factory)`.

items.claim: The modern attrs API was introduced in version 20.1.0.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `define`'s docstring carries `.. versionadded:: 20.1.0`, as do mutable/frozen in the API docs.

items.claim: `_transform_attrs` returns `_Attributes(AttrsClass(attrs), base_attrs, base_attr_map)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The final statement is exactly `return _Attributes(AttrsClass(attrs), base_attrs, base_attr_map)`.

items.claim: `has` checks for the presence of the `__attrs_attrs__` attribute on the class.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `has` does `getattr(cls, "__attrs_attrs__", None)` and returns True if present (also checking generic bases).

items.claim: `make_class` creates the class with `types.new_class(name, bases, {}, lambda ns: ns.update(body))`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: make_class builds the class exactly with `types.new_class(name, bases, {}, lambda ns: ns.update(body))`.

items.claim: If `cache_hash=True` is passed to `@define`, the hash value is computed once and stored on the instance.
items.label: supported
items.reason: With cache_hash the generated `__hash__` computes the hash only if the cache field is None and stores it on the instance.

items.claim: In auto_attribs mode, a class-body value that is not a `_CountingAttr` is wrapped by `attrib(a)` as a default.
items.label: supported
items.reason: In the auto_attribs branch, a class-body value whose class is not `_CountingAttr` is wrapped via `a = attrib(a)`, where the first positional parameter of `attrib` is `default`.

items.claim: The `benchmark` dependency group includes `pytest-codspeed` and `pytest-xdist`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: pyproject.toml was not shown, so the contents of the benchmark dependency group cannot be checked.

items.claim: When fields have no types, the generated init `annotations` dict is just `{'return': None}` because the annotation step requires `a.type` to be non-None.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `annotations` is initialized to `{"return": None}` and entries are only added from `a.type` (or a converter's annotated first param), so untyped fields leave it unchanged.

items.claim: The keyword-only decision in `attrs` is gated on `kw_only` being truthy before `force_kw_only` applies.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `if kw_only:` gates the choice between FORCE/YES (based on force_kw_only), with NO otherwise.

items.claim: `build_class` sets `__attrs_base_of_slotted__ = weakref.ref(cls)` on the original class when building a slotted class.
items.label: supported
items.reason: In the slots branch of build_class, `self._cls.__attrs_base_of_slotted__ = weakref.ref(cls)` is set on the original class.

items.claim: The `auto_exc` parameter defaults to `False` in legacy `attr.s` and `True` in modern `attrs.define`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `attrs()` (attr.s) has `auto_exc=False` while `define()` has `auto_exc=True`.

items.claim: `_make_init_script` merges the defining module's entire `__dict__` into the generated globals if the module is importable.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `if cls.__module__ in sys.modules: globs.update(sys.modules[cls.__module__].__dict__)` merges the module dict into the init globals.

items.claim: In the non-annotated path, attrs sorts the class body fields by the `_CountingAttr` counter.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The non-auto_attribs branch sorts class-dict `_CountingAttr`s with `key=lambda e: e[1].counter`.

items.claim: In `_transform_attrs`, each annotated name is looked up with `a = cd.get(attr_name, NOTHING)`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: The annotated-name lookup is literally `a = cd.get(attr_name, NOTHING)`.

items.claim: `to_bool` maps the integer `1` to `True` and `0` to `False`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `to_bool` returns True for values in a tuple including `1` and False for values including `0`.

items.claim: `asdict` supports a `dict_factory` parameter allowing custom dictionary types such as `OrderedDict`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `asdict` takes a `dict_factory=dict` parameter documented as accepting e.g. `collections.OrderedDict`.

items.claim: `resolve_types` uses `typing.get_type_hints` and accepts `globalns` and `localns` arguments.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `resolve_types(cls, globalns=None, localns=None, ...)` passes those to `typing.get_type_hints`.

items.claim: attrs does not generate a `__ne__`; `add_eq` assigns one shared module-level function.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `add_eq` assigns the module-level `__ne__` function to the class dict rather than generating a per-class one.

items.claim: A class cannot use both `frozen=True` and `on_setattr` hooks; doing so raises a `ValueError` with the message "Frozen classes can't use on_setattr."
items.label: supported
items.reason: `_make_init_script` raises `ValueError("Frozen classes can't use on_setattr.")` when frozen and an on_setattr hook is present.

items.claim: `attr.asdict` converts tuples, sets and frozensets to `list` unless `retain_collection_types` is set.
items.label: supported
items.reason: asdict uses `cf = value_type if retain_collection_types is True else list` for tuple/list/set/frozenset values.

items.claim: Even in the `these` path, `_transform_attrs` calls `_get_annotations` and uses `anns.get(attr_name)` as each field's type.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `anns = _get_annotations(cls)` runs unconditionally before the `these` branch, and `anns.get(attr_name)` is passed for every entry of ca_list.

items.claim: `slots_setstate` accepts either a tuple (for pickles written by attrs before v22.2.0) or a dict, and when given a dict sets only the names actually present.
items.label: supported
items.reason: slots_setstate handles a tuple state for pre-22.2.0 pickles and otherwise only sets names that are `in state`.

items.claim: `_determine_whether_to_implement`, given a None flag and `auto_detect=True`, loops over the dunder names calling `_has_own_attribute`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: With flag None and auto_detect True, the function iterates over *dunders* calling `_has_own_attribute(cls, dunder)`.

items.claim: When `auto_attribs=True`, `_transform_attrs` converts PEP 526 annotations into attributes.
items.label: supported
items.reason: In `_transform_attrs`, when auto_attribs is True it iterates the class annotations and wraps non-_CountingAttr values with `attrib(a)`.

items.claim: attrs security issues should be reported via the Tidelift security contact.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: .github/SECURITY.md was not shown, so the reporting channel cannot be verified.

items.claim: When the class has both `__module__` and `__qualname__`, `_ClassBuilder.__init__` sets `self._add_method_dunders = self._add_method_dunders_unsafe`, the variant that assigns without `contextlib.suppress`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When both attributes exist, the unsafe variant is chosen, and it assigns __module__/__qualname__/__doc__ without contextlib.suppress.

items.claim: In `asdict`, a dict value is rebuilt with `dict_factory` over key/value pairs, with keys processed using `is_key=True`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Dict values are rebuilt via `df = dict_factory` with `_asdict_anything(kk, is_key=True, ...)` for keys.

items.claim: When `init=False`, attrs routes the identical generated script to `__attrs_init__` instead of `__init__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: When added_init is false, add_attrs_init calls the same `_make_init_script` with attrs_init=True, which only switches the method name to `__attrs_init__`.

items.claim: `attr.s` resolves `order` to mirror `eq`, so `make_class` enables ordering by default, while `define` does not.
items.label: supported
items.reason: attr.s mirrors order from eq, make_class passes default_eq=True yielding order=True, whereas define defaults order=False.

items.claim: For a frozen slotted class, `_determine_setters` returns a `_setattr` strategy going through a cached `object.__setattr__`.
items.label: supported
items.reason: For frozen+slots the setters are `_setattr`/`_setattr_with_converter`, which emit calls to the cached `object.__setattr__` bound via `_cached_setattr_get(self)`.

items.claim: `ClassProps.__init__` takes sixteen positional settings and assigns them directly to slots.
items.label: supported
items.reason: ClassProps.__init__ takes exactly the sixteen listed parameters and assigns each directly to the corresponding slot.

items.claim: `fields` calls `get_generic_base` to determine whether the argument is a specialized generic.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `fields` begins with `generic_base = get_generic_base(cls)` and uses it for specialized generics.

items.claim: The coverage job in CI runs `coverage combine` followed by `coverage report --fail-under=100`.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: .github/workflows/ci.yml was not shown, so the coverage job commands cannot be checked.

items.claim: `tests/test_forward_references.py` is ignored on Python versions below 3.14.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: Neither tests/conftest.py nor pyproject.toml (where such an ignore would live) was shown.

items.claim: Since version 21.1.0, the `eq` and `order` field parameters also accept custom callables.
items.label: supported
items.reason: Both `attrib` and `field` docstrings note `.. versionchanged:: 21.1.0 *eq*, *order*, and *cmp* also accept a custom callable`.

items.claim: The attrs AI policy prohibits listing LLM bots in `Co-authored-by` tags.
items.label: unverifiable
items.reason: .github/AI_POLICY.md was not shown, so its rules about Co-authored-by tags cannot be checked.

items.claim: `has()` checks whether a class is an `attrs` class.
items.label: supported
items.reason: `has(cls)` is documented and implemented as checking whether a class is an attrs class.
